blocks.text: A language is made not only of words and rules, but also of phrases already ready: the formulas that are said to those who celebrate, to those who are sick, to those who leave; idiomatic expressions that journalists love ( ⁧حِبْرٌ عَلَى وَرَقٍ⁩ Ink on paper (i.e. dead letter) proverbs that close a speech. In this unit you learn the most important social formulas with their response, about twenty idiomatic expressions frequent in the press, a dozen proverbs with their Italian equivalent and some Egyptian proverb to recognize. Two weeks.

1. use the most common social formulas and respond in the expected way ( ⁧مَبْرُوك⁩ → ⁧اللهُ يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ⁩ );
2. recognize an idiomatic expression and understand its figurative meaning, without translating it to the letter;
3. understand and translate about twenty idioms in the newspapers;
4. recognize ten classical Arab proverbs and their Italian equivalent;
5. use a proverb at the right time, with formulas that introduce it.
